paindrawr: Quantification of pain drawings

Source: R/paindrawr-package.R
paindrawr-package.Rd

Provides tools for importing, processing, quantifying, and visualising digital pain drawings. Pain drawings are commonly used in clinical research to document the location and distribution of pain on a schematic representation of the human body. Digital pain drawings can capture individual pen strokes as x- and y-coordinates, allowing more detailed analyses than traditional region-based classifications. The package supports the reconstruction of individual drawings, quantification of marked areas, anatomical region-based analyses, and the generation of group-level pain heatmaps. It is designed to work with data collected using the 'paindraw' REDCap external module, but also supports data from other sources.

Terminology

TermMeaning
pdr_drawingNamed list for one drawing: .id, .file, .version, .width, .height, .units, .timestamp, .app, .strokes, .points, optional .rgba, .stencil, .stencil_inverted
pdr_listA list of pdr_drawings (typically the list-column pdr_data)
pdr_tibbleA tibble with columns id and a pdr_list column (default name pdr_data)

See pdr_match() for validating and coercing between these types.
